Q1.why: The runner queries every step and adds each chunk; the ensembler keeps the last `chunk` = 10 (deque maxlen), so steps 11..20 all cover step 20 (offsets 9..0). Weights are exp(-m*i) over the list ordered oldest first, so i = 0 is the chunk from step 11.

distractors.A: Reads the weights as favouring the newest prediction (the common ACT misreading).
distractors.C: Assumes chunked execution without ensembling (query every k steps).

Q2.why: align_episode reads the trigger with sync.hold_last (zero-order hold, searchsorted side='right' - 1): at 2.4 s the latest leader sample at or before is still 0; at 2.5 s the 2.437 s sample (1) is the latest.

distractors.A: Assumes the gripper goes through interp_linear like the positions.

Q3.why: action_chunks pads past the end with the last action but sets mask False there; chunk_loss multiplies both the L1 and the BCE terms by the mask. For index T-1 only offset 0 is < T.

distractors.B: Sees the padding but not the mask.
distractors.C: Thinks the mask only applies to the L1 term.
distractors.D: Thinks incomplete chunks are dropped (the docstring says the opposite).

Q4.why: load_demo_data fits Normalizer on train_frames only; fit uses f.obs[f.usable]; save_checkpoint stores normalizer.state_dict(); PolicyRunner.load rebuilds it from the checkpoint. All 7 observation columns are z-scored.

distractors.B: Misses that fit() gets train_frames only.
distractors.C: Mixes up the observation side (all columns) with the action side (gripper column left alone).

Q5.why: align_episode raises Rejected('only 3.xx s where all streams have data') because the common window is under DataConfig.min_window_s = 4.0. Its camera gap (~0.045 s) and detection rate are fine. Holds for the shipped code and the reference fix alike.

distractors.D: Validation episodes do produce samples (the val tensors).

Q6.why: The bench returns (NaN, False) on a dropout; PolicyRunner.act keeps self._last_block from the last detected frame and builds the observation from it. Training used sync.interp_valid, which interpolates between valid frames, so train and run time differ slightly here.

distractors.B: Assumes run time can do what the offline pipeline does (it would need a future frame).
distractors.D: There is no skip path; the network is queried every step.

Q7.why: rollout calls runner.reset(), which clears the history; _push then fills all obs_horizon slots with the first observation. chunking.obs_history clips indices to 0, so frame 0 repeats in training too.

distractors.B: Stale state across resets would happen without reset(); rollout calls it.
